## Introduction


A bonus gift card promotion looks like the margin-friendly cousin of a discount. The shopper pays full price for a gift card, gets a bonus card on top, and nobody sees a percentage off on the product page.


But the bonus still has to be paid for. It just gets paid for later, in product.


The comparisons that rank today tend to stop at two options, the bonus gift card and the discount code. This one adds a third column, the conditional cashback rebate that[Playably](https://playably.ai/) runs for Shopify brands.


With cashback, shoppers pay full price, and if a real, published trigger event hits, Playably pays them 100% of their order back by Venmo or PayPal. The brand pays $0 of the rebate.


It's our blog, so we have a horse in this race. We'll still tell you where the other two win.


### Key Takeaways


- A bonus gift card promotion delays the cost of a discount rather than removing it.
- A discount code cuts margin at checkout, on every order that uses it.
- Playably's conditional cashback keeps full price, and the brand pays $0 of the rebate.
- Gift card bonuses return as store credit, while Playably cashback pays out as money.
- Pick by who funds the reward and when the cost lands on your books.


## What a Bonus Gift Card Promotion Is


A bonus gift card promotion rewards a gift card purchase with extra value. A typical version reads "buy a $100 gift card, get a $20 bonus card," with the numbers set by the brand.


The shopper pays the full face value of the gift card. The bonus card is store credit they spend on a later order, often with an expiry date or a minimum spend set by the brand.


It is popular in the holiday window for a reason. It brings cash in now and pulls a second visit into the new year.


If you're weighing it as a holiday promotion, our[Q4 marketing calendar](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/q4-marketing-calendar) lays out the dates around it.


## How a Discount Code Works on Margin


A discount code is the simplest lever there is. The shopper enters it, the price drops, and the cost lands on that order immediately.


It's fast, it's easy to set up, and it converts. Plenty of brands use codes well, and there are moments where a code is the right call.


The cost is that the cut comes out of margin on every order that uses it. Run codes often enough and shoppers can learn to wait for the next one, which our piece on[discount fatigue](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/discount-fatigue) covers in depth.


## Where Conditional Cashback Fits as the Third Option


A conditional cashback rebate works differently from both. Shoppers buy at full price and get auto-entered, with no code to remember.


If a real, published trigger hits, Playably pays them 100% of their order back, directly. Playably insures and hedges the payout, so you keep your full margin and pay $0 of the rebate.


The trigger is a moment your shoppers already care about. Playably publishes a library of pre-modelled[moments across sports, weather and culture](https://playably.ai/pages/upcoming-offers) , and adds new ones weekly.


Cashback is paid to the shopper as money through Venmo or PayPal, usually within days. It is not store credit or a gift card.

For the margin math on a single order, our breakdown of[cash back vs discount codes](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/cash-back-vs-discount-codes) goes deeper on the per-order math.


## How the Three Compare on Margin


### Price at checkout


A discount lowers the price the shopper pays. A bonus gift card keeps the gift card at face value, but the bonus card is a discount on a future order.


Conditional cashback keeps full price at checkout, and nothing comes off later. Shoppers buy at full price, so you protect margin instead of discounting to it.


### Who carries the cost


With a code or a gift card bonus, the brand funds the reward. What changes is the timing.


With Playably, the brand pays $0 of the rebate. Playably carries the payout so your store never books the liability, and your exposure is a small, fixed amount agreed in advance.


### What the shopper remembers


A code is forgotten at checkout. A bonus card is remembered when it's spent, or when it expires unused.


A rebate tied to a real moment gives the shopper something to watch. You get the brand halo of the moment everyone's watching without paying to sponsor it.


Our guide to[what conditional rebate promotions cost](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/conditional-rebate-promotions-for-ecommerce-in-2026-who-runs-them-who-pays-out-and-what-they-cost) explains who runs them and who pays out.


## When Each Offer Makes Sense


**A discount code** fits a fast clearance, a single loyal segment, or a moment where speed beats margin. It is the easiest lever to pull.


**A bonus gift card promotion** fits a brand that wants cash in December and a return visit in January, and can carry the bonus as future store credit.


**Conditional cashback** fits a brand that wants full-price conversion without booking any payout. Playably prices on performance, so you only pay when a sale happens.

The strongest argument for the third column is what it has returned at full price.


Soul CBD's OVERTIME Big Game Cashback campaign saw 59% of campaign buyers subscribe, compared with 41% of other shoppers that same week. Baskets were 16% bigger than the rest of the store, at $99 against $86.


Jordan Craig's NFL Draft rebate ran 2.5× more cost-efficient than the brand's own Easter and Tax Day sales. The[Jordan Craig case study](https://playably.ai/pages/jordancraig-case-study) has the full results.


Buckle Me Baby Coats saw sales jump 23% on launch and participant AOV rise 40%, and never touched its price. Playably says it has launched 30 or more Shopify brands with 100% retention.


Playably was featured in Inc. for its risk hedged rebate model, and the[Inc. feature recap](https://playably.ai/blogs/about-gamification/playably-featured-inc) explains how the brand hands off the risk.


## Conclusion


A bonus gift card promotion protects margin at checkout and gives some of it back later, as store credit. A discount code gives it back on the spot.


Conditional cashback is the option where the price holds and the brand pays nothing toward the rebate. Shoppers pay full price, Playably insures and hedges the payout, and a real moment decides whether they get 100% of their order back.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Does a bonus gift card promotion protect margin better than a discount?


A bonus gift card promotion protects margin at checkout better than a discount, because the gift card sells at face value. The bonus card still costs the brand product when it is redeemed, so the margin hit moves to a later order. Playably's conditional cashback keeps full price with no later cost, because Playably insures and hedges the payout and the brand pays $0 of the rebate.


### Is Playably cashback paid as a gift card or store credit?


Playably cashback is paid to the shopper as money through Venmo or PayPal, usually within days, not as store credit or a gift card. Playably pays it directly, which is why the brand pays $0 of the rebate and keeps full margin. When the trigger hits, shoppers get 100% of their order back rather than a voucher to spend with the brand again.


### How is a conditional cashback rebate different from a bonus gift card promotion?


A conditional cashback rebate differs from a bonus gift card promotion in who pays and how the shopper is rewarded. With a bonus gift card, the brand funds store credit for a future order. With Playably's conditional rebate, shoppers buy at full price and get 100% of their order back by Venmo or PayPal if a real, published trigger hits, and Playably carries the payout.


### Who pays the cashback compared with the bonus on a gift card promotion?


The brand pays the bonus on a gift card promotion, in product, when the bonus card is spent. Playably pays the cashback on a conditional rebate. Playably insures and hedges the payout, so the brand keeps its full margin and pays $0 of the rebate, and Playably carries the payout so the store never books the liability.


### When should a Shopify brand choose cashback over a bonus gift card promotion?


A Shopify brand should choose cashback over a bonus gift card promotion when it wants full-price conversion without owing anything back later. Playably's conditional rebate holds the price, pays shoppers in money rather than store credit, and prices on performance, so the brand only pays when a sale happens. A gift card bonus still suits brands that want December cash and a January return visit.
